This module implements a thread-safe Least Recently Used (LRU) cache that
automatically expires entries after a configurable time-to-live (TTL).

- LRU eviction policy: when the cache exceeds its capacity, the least

  proactively removed to keep the cache lean.

    cache.set("key1", "value1")   # survives for up to 5 minutes
    cache.get("key1")             # returns "value1"
    cache.delete("key1")
"""

     used* entry is evicted before the new entry is added.

   * Every stored value is paired with an absolute expiration timestamp
     (`expires_at`).  A background ``Thread`` periodically sweeps the

     all shared mutable state.

   * The public API of ``LRUCache`` is protected by a single ``threading.RLock``.
     This guarantees that concurrent reads and writes never corrupt the
     internal data structures (list nodes, dict mapping, lock state).

time-to-live (TTL) expiry. The cache is implemented using a thread-safe
lock to ensure safe concurrent access from multiple threads.

Key Features:
- LRU eviction policy based on access order.
- Per-item TTL (time-to-live) support; entries expire automatically.
- Thread-safe operations via a reentrant lock (`threading.RLock`).
- A robust pytest suite to verify correctness, TTL behavior, and
  thread-safety.

Design Overview
---------------
The cache is built on top of two standard library collections:
- `OrderedDict` (Python 3.7+): Used to maintain insertion/access order.
- `threading.RLock`: Protects the internal data structures.

Each entry in the cache stores:
    key:        The lookup key (hashable).
    value:      The cached payload (picklable).
    expiry:     Absolute time (float timestamp) when the entry expires.
    inserted_at: Timestamp when the entry was first created.
    accessed_at: Timestamp when the entry was last accessed.

When an item is accessed (get or set), the `accessed_at` timestamp is
updated and the item is moved to the "most recently used" position via
`OrderedDict.move_to_end`.

The LRU eviction policy works as follows:
1. When the cache reaches its `max_items` capacity, the oldest item
   (the one at the front of the `OrderedDict`) is considered for eviction.
2. If that item has already expired, it is simply removed.
3. Otherwise, it is removed and a new item is inserted.

external libraries beyond the standard library (``threading``,

  O(1) move-to-end (`popitem(last=False)` and explicit reordering) which we
  use to satisfy the LRU semantics.

  raw payload together with:

  whose TTL has elapsed and removes them.  The thread is daemonised so it
  does not prevent interpreter shutdown.
* All public methods are guarded by a single ``threading.Lock`` to guarantee
  thread-safe access even while the expiry thread mutates the internal
  ``OrderedDict``.

Complexity analysis
-------------------
* ``get`` / ``put`` – O(1) amortised.
* TTL expiry check – O(n) where n is the number of entries, performed
  infrequently by the background thread.
